response: {"title":"Atomic requirement parsing","intervention":"Treat every independently testable clause in the user request as a separate acceptance criterion, including clauses joined by conjunctions, and implement each criterion before stopping.","claim":"On matched fixed-deadline Python tasks with requirements dispersed across modules, appending this instruction will improve complete-task pass_rate versus no appended instruction with no more than a 10% increase in median wall_time or turns.","mechanism":"Splitting compound language into atomic acceptance criteria prevents one implemented clause from masking an omitted sibling clause during planning and completion judgment.","assumptions":["Most target requirements are expressible as independently testable clauses.","The agent can distinguish requirement conjunctions from explanatory prose."],"risks":["Over-segmentation may turn one coherent behavior into redundant work.","Ambiguous clauses may be incorrectly promoted to mandatory scope.","More acceptance criteria may encourage shallow coverage when the deadline is tight."],"test_plan":{"experiment":"Assign matched multi-module Python tasks at random to identical agents with either this appended instruction or no appended instruction and enforce the same deadline.","metrics":["pass_rate","wall_time","turns"],"success_condition":"The treatment produces a higher all-criteria pass_rate while treatment median wall_time and turns are each at most 110% of control."},"single_shot_ordinal":3}
